newsitem.title: USA: Dakota, Minnesota railroad sets $1.2 bln project.
newsitem.headline: Dakota, Minnesota railroad sets $1.2 bln project.

text.p: Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Railroad Corp said Monday it plans to build approximately 250 miles of new railroad to extend its existing line into the Powder River Basin in Wyoming as part of a $1.2 billion project.
It also will rebuild about 650 miles of existing track to meet what it called modern standards.
Dakota, Minnesota said this $1.2 billion project is scheduled to be completed within five years.
Dakota, Minnesota said the project would transform it into a Class-I railroad. Class-I railroads are the largest lines.
The Powder River Basin contains one of the richest deposits of low-sulfur coal in the world.

"There is rapidly growing demand for the Powder River Basin's inexpensive, environmentally friendly, low-sulfur coal," Kevin Schieffer, president, said in a statement. "Implementation of Phase II of the Clean Air Act Amendments affects all coal-fired power plants, mandating additional reductions in sulfur emissions."
Schieffer added that a team of outside economists studied the economic impact of the proposed project and estimated there would be substantial benefits in Minnesota, South Dakota and Wyoming.

He added that the project is expected to create over 6,500 construction-related jobs with earnings of $215 million per year for two years, and generate $52 million in state taxes during construction in Wyoming, South Dakota and Minnesota.
"This project is just too compelling to not get done," J. Michael Buchanan, managing director of Lombard Investments Inc of San Francisco, said in a statement.

Lombard Investments formed Dakota, Minnesota in 1986, and represents the interests of the majority institutional shareholders. Buchanan said no shareholders have taken dividends since the founding of the railroad, choosing instead to reinvest over $100 million in track, cars and locomotives.

The railroad said it was approached by a number of parties who have expressed an interest in participating in this project. Morgan Stanley was retained to assist in identifying strategic partners for Dakota, Minnesota's expansion into the Powder River Basin and rebuilding of the existing track.
The railroad said the new construction project will be subject to approval of the federal Surface Transportation Board.
Schieffer said the new project will allow the railroad to serve current and future shippers better, while enabling the company to strengthen its finances and grow its business.

"Rebuilding the line will enable us to significantly reduce transit time across our current system," he added. "In 1996, average mainline transit time was approximately 150 hours. This project will reduce that time to approximately 17 hours, providing our customers greatly improved service and enhanced access to the major markets in the Midwest."
